# Sirach Chapter 35 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 35 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_035_page_001.jpg

---

**35:1** Living by God's instruction is itself an act of worship — it's worth more than many sacrifices. Keeping the commandments is like offering a peace offering.

**35:2** Showing gratitude is like bringing a grain offering; giving generously to those in need is a thank offering in itself.

**35:3** Turning away from evil pleases the Lord; turning away from wrongdoing makes atonement for sin.

**35:4** Never come before the Lord empty-handed — all of this is what the commandments require.

**35:5** The offering of someone who does right enriches the altar; its fragrance rises up before the Most High.

**35:6** The sacrifice of a just person is acceptable to God, and the memory of it will never be lost.

**35:7** Give generously to honor the Lord, and don't hold back the firstfruits of your labor.

**35:8** When you bring an offering, do it with a smile. Give your tithe joyfully.

**35:9** Give back to the Most High in proportion to what he has given you — generously, as your means allow.

**35:10** For the Lord is a God who pays back, and he will repay you seven times over.

**35:11** Don't try to bribe him — he won't take it. Don't put your trust in an offering made from dishonest gain. The Lord is the judge, and he plays no favorites.

**35:12** He shows no bias against the poor, and he hears the prayer of those who have been wronged.

**35:13** He doesn't ignore the cry of the orphan, or the widow pouring out her complaint.

**35:14** Look at the tears streaming down the widow's face — doesn't her cry go up against the one who put them there?

**35:15** Whoever serves God with a whole heart will be welcomed, and that person's prayer will reach the very clouds.

**35:16** The prayer of the humble breaks through the clouds; it keeps going until it arrives — it doesn't stop until the Most High takes notice

**35:17** and does justice for the righteous, carrying out judgment. The Lord won't delay; he won't keep holding back,

**35:18** until he has broken the power of the pitiless and brought nations to account; until he has swept away the arrogant in their multitudes and shattered the scepters of oppressors;

**35:19** until he has repaid everyone exactly what they deserve, their deeds judged by the intentions behind them; until he has vindicated his own people and filled them with joy at his mercy.

**35:20** In a time of trouble, mercy is as welcome as rain in a drought.
